title: Runbooks
heading: Create a procedure
text:
Create a procedure
Read the [authoring policy](authoring.md#creation-and-follow-up), choose one real condition, and copy the template. Identify ownership, triggers, required access, verifiable preconditions, bounded diagnosis/actions, recovery verification, and stop/escalation conditions. Do not invent provider commands.

title: Runbooks
heading: Find related policy
text:
Find related policy
[Health checks](../reliability/health-checks.md) and [observability](../reliability/observability.md) for diagnostic evidence.
[Alerting](../reliability/alerting.md) for actionable signals and runbook references.
[Secrets](../security/secrets-management.md), [classification](../security/data-classification.md), and [retention](../security/data-retention.md) for safe handling of credentials, evidence, and temporary exports.
[Documentation task index](../README.md) for other current policies.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Runbook: Procedure Title
text:
Runbook: Procedure Title
**Owner:** actual responsible owner
**Status:** active only after the procedure exists and is verified
**Environment / applicability:**
**Related alerts:**
**Required access:**
Follow [authoring policy](authoring.md), [production access](../security/production-access.md), [incident response](../security/incident-response.md), and [redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md). Replace prompts with current, verified details; this template is not an executable procedure or an authorization grant.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Purpose
text:
Purpose
State the one operational condition or task handled by this procedure.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Trigger / Symptoms
text:
Trigger / Symptoms
Identify observable alerts, errors, or symptoms that activate the procedure, and cases where it must not be used.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Impact
text:
Impact
Describe affected capabilities, scope, urgency, and data/security risk, including any known limit on impact.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Preconditions
text:
Preconditions
Verify the target environment and observed condition.
Verify required access and authorization for the planned actions.
Verify procedure-specific safety conditions and current state.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Diagnosis
text:
Diagnosis
Order low-risk inspection before mutation: relevant metrics, alerts, logs, traces, errors, and bounded read-only checks. Establish affected scope and whether deployment, migration, configuration, or dependency changes contributed. Include expected results and evidence-based branches. Add provider commands only when tooling exists; continue only while evidence matches the procedure.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Mitigation / Procedure
text:
Mitigation / Procedure
Write ordered, bounded, copyable actions with consequences, expected output, decision points, and temporary-measure removal needs. Before a destructive, irreversible, or high-risk action, explain the exact affected scope and consequences. Stop when observed state differs from the documented scope.
State whether actions are safe to repeat and how to inspect an unknown outcome before retrying. For long-running work, specify supported batch size, progress, monitoring, pause/resume, failure recovery, and concurrent-execution limits.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Prove the intended service, security, or data state through relevant health, errors, latency, progress, integrity, authorization, revocation, or application behavior. A successful command or cleared alert alone is insufficient. Name any justified post-recovery observation period and signals.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Rollback / Recovery
text:
Rollback / Recovery
Describe safe reversal and its compatibility prerequisites, or the actual forward-recovery path when rollback is unsafe/impossible. Identify irreversible effects. Remove this section only when it does not apply.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Escalation
text:
Escalation
Stop when evidence does not match, scope exceeds bounds, access/preconditions cannot be verified, destructive impact is unknown, corruption/compromise is suspected, recovery fails, or postconditions cannot be verified. Preserve safe evidence and identify the real escalation owner when one exists.

title: Runbook: Procedure Title
heading: Follow-Up
text:
Follow-Up
Record needed permanent correction, regression tests, alert/observability changes, automation, temporary-measure removal, runbook update, ADR, or post-incident review. Give follow-up work an owner; keep incident history outside this current procedure.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
text:
Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
**Owner:** IA-MNS project owner (Meta Business Portfolio administrator for the Meta steps)
**Status:** draft — the application side (configuration, webhook verification, signatures, authorization, processing, switch and revocation) is exercised by the synthetic tests in `apps/api/test/whatsapp.test.ts` and the local simulator; no step has run against Meta or the production host yet
**Environment / applicability:** a production host prepared by [host setup and first deployment](production-host-setup-and-first-deployment.md), with IA-MNS identity configured and an active owner
**Related alerts:** none yet; see [observability](../domains/whatsapp-channel.md#observability)
**Required access:** Meta Business Portfolio administrator; an attributable sudo account on the host; an IA-MNS owner session with the second factor
Follow [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets](../security/secrets-management.md) and [incident response](../security/incident-response.md). The [WhatsApp channel domain](../domains/whatsapp-channel.md) owns behavior; [ADR-0036](../adr/0036-add-whatsapp-as-an-agent-channel-authorized-by-owner-linked-numbers.md) owns the decision. Meta's dashboard changes over time: follow its current wording, and stop if a step no longer matches the [Cloud API documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/).

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Purpose
text:
Purpose
Turn the WhatsApp channel on with the dedicated number, revoke one person's access at once, and turn the channel off or remove it.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Trigger / Symptoms
text:
Trigger / Symptoms
Activation: [PH-32 to PH-35](../project/human-actions.md#ph-32) are complete.
Revocation: a linked phone is lost, stolen, transferred, returned, recycled, or the person no longer needs access.
Rollback: unexpected answers or recipients, Meta account problems, cost above expectation, or a security incident.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Impact
text:
Impact
Activation lets linked people query IA-MNS from WhatsApp with their own permissions; answers with business data transit Meta and stay on their devices. Turning the switch off stops every reply that has not reached Meta; nothing else in IA-MNS changes. Removing the configuration and restarting removes the webhook routes (Meta retries undelivered notifications for up to 36 hours, then drops them).

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Preconditions
text:
Preconditions
PH-32 to PH-35 are recorded as complete in [human actions](../project/human-actions.md), including the owner's approval of the Meta processing boundary.
`sudo ia-mns-deploy status` is healthy on a release that contains the WhatsApp module (migrations `202610130001` to `202610130004` applied).
The public origin answers over HTTPS with a certificate Meta accepts; the webhook URL is `https://<IA_MNS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN host>/api/whatsapp/webhook`.
The values are at hand without printing them: phone number ID, WhatsApp Business Account ID, system-user access token, app secret, and a new verify token (`openssl rand -base64 48 | tr -d '/+=' | cut -c1-48`).

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Diagnosis
text:
Diagnosis
`sudo ia-mns-deploy check-config` names missing or inconsistent WhatsApp keys without showing values (all four of `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` and `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`, plus identity and the database).
Logs: `whatsapp_verification_refused` (verify token mismatch), `whatsapp_signature_refused` (wrong app secret or a forged request), `whatsapp_webhook_received` with `refused` counts (sender not linked, disabled, or switch off), `whatsapp_access_token_rejected` (token expired or revoked), `whatsapp_reply_settled` with `outcome` and Meta `code`.
**Administração → Pessoas → (person) → WhatsApp** shows the linked number and whether a message from it was ever accepted.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Mitigation / Procedure
text: Mitigation / Procedure

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Activate
text:
Activate
In `/etc/ia-mns/runtime.env` (`sudo nano`), uncomment and set `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, `WHATSAPP_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` and `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`. Keep `IA_MNS_WHATSAPP_CHANNEL` unset or `disabled`; optionally lower `WHATSAPP_DAILY_LIMIT` for the first days.
`sudo ia-mns-deploy check-config && sudo ia-mns-deploy restart`. Expected: healthy status; `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook` without parameters answers 403 (the route exists).
In the Meta app, configure the WhatsApp webhook with the callback URL above and the same verify token, then subscribe to the `messages` field. Expected: Meta reports the verification as successful and the log shows `whatsapp_verification_accepted`.
In IA-MNS, **Administração → Pessoas**, link the number of one pilot person (preferably the owner's tester with narrow grants). Use international form; Brazilian mobiles need the ninth digit.
In **Administração → Parâmetros → Canais**, set **Atendimento pelo WhatsApp** to **Ligado**.
From the pilot phone, send `/ajuda`, then a question such as *quanto vendemos ontem?*.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Revoke one person
text:
Revoke one person
**Administração → Pessoas → (person) → WhatsApp → Remover número do WhatsApp → Remover número.** Effective at once, including answers being prepared.
If the person must also lose web access, **Desativar** the person (this also refuses WhatsApp) and **Encerrar sessões**.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Roll back the channel
text:
Roll back the channel
Immediate: set **Atendimento pelo WhatsApp** to **Desligado** (no restart). Webhooks keep being acknowledged; nothing is stored or answered and queued replies are revoked.
Complete removal: comment out the five `WHATSAPP_*` values in `runtime.env`, `sudo ia-mns-deploy check-config && sudo ia-mns-deploy restart`, then in the Meta app unsubscribe the webhook (or remove its URL) so Meta stops retrying.
Credential exposure: also revoke the system-user token and reset the app secret in Meta, then follow [secret rotation](production-secret-rotation.md) before reactivating.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Activation: the pilot receives the `/ajuda` text and an answer that matches the same question on the web for the same person and source; the conversation appears on the web with the `WA` mark; **Pessoas** shows the first message as received; `whatsapp_reply_settled` shows `accepted` and later status webhooks.
A number that is not linked receives nothing and the log shows it only as a refused count.
Revocation: a message from the removed number produces no reply and no inbound row (`refused` increases).
Rollback: with the switch off, a test message gets no reply; after removing the configuration, `GET /api/whatsapp/webhook` answers 404.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Rollback / Recovery
text:
Rollback / Recovery
Turning the switch back on or restoring the configuration reactivates the channel; links, history and audit are kept. Messages sent while the channel was off are not processed later. A reply recorded as `unknown` is never resent automatically; the answer remains in the person's web history.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Escalation
text:
Escalation
Stop and escalate (incident response) if a reply reaches a number that is not linked, if a person receives another person's data, if signatures fail for genuine Meta deliveries after the app secret was verified, or if Meta flags the number or account. Keep the switch off while investigating.

title: Runbook: WhatsApp Channel Activation, Revocation and Rollback
heading: Follow-Up
text:
Follow-Up
Record activation evidence in PJ-48 and the related human actions. Add alerts for `whatsapp_access_token_rejected`, sustained `unknown` or `failed` reply outcomes and the daily ceiling once production telemetry exists.

title: AI Data Processing
heading: AI Data Processing
text:
AI Data Processing
This policy owns the provider-transmission boundary for IA-MNS business analysis. It complements [classification](data-classification.md), [authorization](authorization.md), [retention](data-retention.md), [telemetry redaction](telemetry-redaction.md), and [ERP access](erp-database-access.md). The implementation owners are the [evidence projector](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/evidence.ts), [text safeguard](../../apps/api/src/ai/transmission-text.ts), and [conversation orchestrator](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/conversation.ts).

title: AI Data Processing
heading: Approved purpose and data categories
text:
Approved purpose and data categories
On 2026-10-12 the project owner explicitly authorized reuse of the existing OpenAI API credential for synthetic evaluations and transmission of real business data needed for authorized IA-MNS analyses. The approval includes sales, products, revenue and operational details where justified; it does not authorize indiscriminate extraction, credentials, unnecessary personal data, or processing without applicable corporate and legal authority. There is no per-query approval requirement within that scope.
Category
Current provider policy
Reviewed sales totals, comparisons, period/product breakdowns, product registration and classification
Allowed within current actor permissions, selected ERP, bounded tools and evidence projection. A detailed read needs an analytical purpose; it cannot expand database privileges.
ERP buyer, supplier or other dimension values classified as personal in the semantic catalog
Candidate names and resolved personal values are withheld from provider evidence. Authorized users can still choose the numbered result card locally; a personal filter does not disable the remaining sales analysis.
User-authored text and filter words
Necessary bounded conversation context, subject to recognizable secret/identifier redaction. Existing resolver interpretation can receive names the user types; this is not authorization to retrieve or disclose additional personal records. Avoid supplying unnecessary personal details.
Sensitive personal data, individual employee/customer records, banking/payment credentials
No approved analysis tool or transmission projection. Keep the affected category unavailable until the controller establishes purpose, authority, safeguards and a reviewed field contract. Other approved categories remain available.
Authentication secrets, passwords, keys, tokens, connection credentials
Prohibited in model context, answers, traces, test fixtures and generated artifacts. The API key is used only as transport authentication.
Unknown result payloads, arbitrary database JSON, raw schema dumps
Denied by the evidence projector. Adding a capability requires a deliberate field projection, classification and deny-path tests.
Business confidentiality and personal-data status are separate. An aggregate may still identify a natural person in context, and pseudonyms do not establish anonymity. A newly introduced dimension must declare its real meaning and privacy constraints before activation.

title: AI Data Processing
heading: Enforced transmission controls
text:
Enforced transmission controls
The server validates existing sales/product contracts and explicitly constructs provider evidence. It never forwards entire entities or arbitrary capability `result` objects. Source identity and selection provenance are checked; each ERP retains its own section, basis, units, periods and totals. Selection identifiers and totals cannot be reused as if they belonged to the other ERP.
The initial context is a bounded summary. `business-evidence/1` currently permits at most twelve rows for context, forty for analysis and one hundred for justified detail across a projection, with a 48,000-byte evidence ceiling and four hundred numeric facts. These are transmission limits, independent of the stricter source-query and whole-turn budgets. Totals are deterministic complete-scope values from the source result; bounded rows are explicitly marked incomplete. Omitted detail is never zero or evidence of absence. Oversized or malformed payloads are withheld rather than forwarded unboundedly.
Facts retain exact decimal strings, dates, units, source and meaning. The model can use their values to reason; the final response binds quantitative claims to server-owned fact references. Formatting never converts financial decimals through binary floating-point. These controls prevent invented numeric values from replacing supplied facts; they do not prove that every qualitative inference is correct. Conversational evaluations remain necessary.
Reading stored evidence checks current permissions, registered capability policy and all inherited dependencies. Derived prose and its retained evidence snapshots inherit the union of permissions for information supplied to the model, including information it did not cite. Revocation therefore applies to summaries as well as original result cards. The actor-owned conversation remains the authoritative context store.
Personal product fields are identified through the reviewed semantic catalog, not guessed from names. Unrecognized dimension titles or obsolete catalog versions cannot expose resolved personal values. The projector omits unstructured semantic-selection descriptions that may contain a person's words, while preserving catalog version and the fact that a selection was applied. Normal product/classification labels are treated as untrusted data. Recognizable secret and identifier patterns and control delimiters receive additional text safeguards. This is defense in depth, **not a universal personal-data detector or a proof against prompt injection**. Tool permissions, source binding, reviewed query compilation and output checks remain authoritative even when a label contains hostile instructions.

title: AI Data Processing
heading: Provider controls and verification boundary
text:
Provider controls and verification boundary
The repository uses foreground Responses calls with `store:false`, bounded output and no automatic retries. It keeps conversation state locally instead of depending on provider conversation storage. OpenAI documentation states that API data is not used for training by default. Standard abuse-monitoring retention can still be up to thirty days; `store:false` is not Zero Data Retention. ZDR and Modified Abuse Monitoring require account eligibility and approval, and feature exceptions apply. Prompt caching and image/file processing have additional retention behavior. Data residency depends on the selected region, endpoint, model and project controls. [OpenAI data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data).
Code inspection verifies request settings only. This change does **not** verify this organization's training-sharing opt-ins, signed processing terms, subprocessors, retention-control approval, selected residency region or regional inference. The accountable owner must record those account and contractual facts before asserting them to customers or enabling a category that depends on them. No ZDR, Brazilian residency or unconditional deletion guarantee is claimed. Ordinary authorized nonpersonal business analysis does not wait for a personal-data category's separate legal approval.
Provider-hosted files, vector stores, background processing, remote MCP tools, web connectors and hosted execution are separate processing boundaries. The sales/product evidence path does not enable them. Any attachment feature must document its actual extraction location, data-category gate, purpose, retention and deletion; a filename, extension or model classification alone is insufficient. Raw images can include faces, documents and embedded text, so controls must address the content sent, not only extracted text. The implemented [attachment path](../architecture/conversational-autonomy.md#attachments-and-presentation-preferences) requires an explicit operational classification, purpose and absence-of-restricted-data assertion. It rejects recognizable secrets in text, strips image metadata, validates bounded envelopes and transmits content only through a requested read tool. Text classification and image pixels retain residual content risk; neither the extension nor that assertion proves anonymity. Unsupported formats and restricted categories remain unavailable.

title: AI Data Processing
heading: WhatsApp delivery boundary
text:
WhatsApp delivery boundary
The [WhatsApp channel](../domains/whatsapp-channel.md) does not change what the agent sends to the model: the same projection and controls apply to its turns. It adds a separate recipient of the **answers**: replies to linked people are delivered through Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform and remain on their devices. Only the answer text (with its server-rendered facts) is sent; ERP queries, evidence snapshots and other people's data are not. Activation requires the owner's approval of this boundary ([PH-35](../project/human-actions.md#ph-35)).

title: AI Data Processing
heading: LGPD and international transfer responsibilities
text:
LGPD and international transfer responsibilities
The LGPD applies to information about an identified or identifiable natural person. Before adding a personal-data category, the controller must record purpose and necessity, an applicable legal basis, access restrictions, transparency, subject-rights handling and retention. Sensitive data has distinct legal grounds. The law also requires processing records and appropriate security; applicable impact-assessment and incident duties must be evaluated for the concrete operation. The project owner's authorization is a product-scope decision, not substitute consent from every data subject or proof that a particular legal basis applies. [LGPD, articles 5–7, 11, 18, 33, 37–38 and 46–48](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2018/lei/l13709compilado.htm).
For personal data transferred abroad, establish both the processing legal basis and an applicable international-transfer mechanism. ANPD Resolution 19/2024 addresses adequacy and contractual mechanisms; its standard clauses must be adopted in the prescribed form when that mechanism is used. The regulation also requires transparency and minimum necessary transfer scope. Its twelve-month contractual adaptation period is not a new grace period created by this implementation. Do not assume foreign clauses, generic provider terms or a DPA automatically establish the required Brazilian mechanism. The controller/legal owner must verify the applicable contract and ANPD decisions, including amendments, for the actual recipient and transfer. [ANPD Resolution 19/2024](https://www.gov.br/anpd/pt-br/acesso-a-informacao/institucional/atos-normativos/regulamentacoes_anpd/resolucao-cd-anpd-no-19-de-23-de-agosto-de-2024).
The remaining corporate review is category-scoped: identify controller/operator responsibilities and any subprocessors; confirm contracts, confidentiality restrictions and international-transfer terms; record the personal-data purpose/legal basis and notices; define retention/deletion and incident contacts; assess whether further review is needed for sensitive or high-risk processing. Keep only the affected unapproved category blocked. This document records technical requirements and verified implementation, not a finding that all corporate or legal obligations have been satisfied.

title: AI Data Processing
heading: Traceability, retention and evaluation
text:
Traceability, retention and evaluation
The projection returns an allowlisted audit envelope: policy version, purpose class, selected source, permission dependencies, section/row/byte counts, truncation and redaction counts. The orchestrator records bounded metadata with the turn correlation; analytical justification, labels, values, prompt text, model responses and snapshots must not enter ordinary logs. Conversational execution caps content tracing at metadata, including nested tools; debug settings cannot enable capture of newly exposed financial evidence. Existing confidential debug workflows remain subject to the [redaction policy](telemetry-redaction.md).
Persisted result snapshots and generated summaries are confidential conversation content. They follow actor ownership and the existing conversation deletion path. Deleting an IA-MNS conversation cannot guarantee deletion of provider abuse-monitoring copies or expired-backup contents; the deployment's retention schedule remains an owner responsibility under [retention](data-retention.md). Real business conversations are not automatically approved evaluation or training datasets. Curated tests and provider evaluations use synthetic data; captures remain in their controlled local workflow and require separate review before promotion.
The [evidence tests](../../apps/api/test/agent-evidence.test.ts) exercise exact decimal/date references, inherited permission denial, semantic product dependencies, unknown-field rejection, source isolation, multi-panel references, detail limits, personal option suppression, retained snapshots and recognizable-secret redaction. Passing them establishes those boundaries, not universal classification, legal compliance or correctness of every possible model inference.

title: Authentication
heading: Authentication
text:
Authentication
This policy owns trusted identity, credential, and session requirements. [Authorization](authorization.md) owns permission decisions; [secrets management](secrets-management.md) owns credential lifecycle and [redaction](telemetry-redaction.md) owns telemetry handling. Start with the [task index](../README.md) for other concerns.

title: Authentication
heading: Current implementation and scope
text:
Current implementation and scope
The API verifies JWT bearer access tokens according to [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) when token settings are configured. The shared [verifier](../../apps/api/src/authentication.ts) is the executable source for accepted claims and algorithms; it yields a principal ID and issuer scopes, and each module maps scopes to its own capabilities. The [API README](../../apps/api/README.md) describes configuration and the current token contract; the [web README](../../apps/web/README.md) describes the in-memory credential boundary.
IA-MNS implements its own identity under [ADR-0022](../adr/0022-own-the-ia-mns-identity-with-verified-external-links.md) and [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-serve-one-frontend-to-three-surfaces-with-host-identity-proofs.md): an in-process issuer of ES256 access tokens verified by the same ADR-0012 verifier, local accounts (scrypt, TOTP, recovery codes), rotating refresh sessions in HttpOnly cookies for the direct URL, cookie-free embedded sessions renewed by host proofs, and links to PDT Connect and Sankhya identities proven server-side. The [identity domain](../domains/identity.md) owns the current flows, limits and deployment requirements. Requirements below still govern any change; they do not imply that unlisted mechanisms exist. Do not reopen the accepted JWT decision by treating the first API's token format or verification library as undecided.
The current verifier rejects invalid credentials without disclosing token details. Key retrieval, malformed trusted JWKS data, and unexpected verifier failures raise a separate availability error; the API returns a safe 503 and records bounded diagnostics. This distinguishes an authentication infrastructure failure from a routine invalid token while still failing closed. Session refresh and revocation for IA-MNS tokens are implemented by the identity module; external provider readiness is tracked in the repository's human-action checklist (linked from the README's [Current state](../../README.md#current-state)).
